The '''2018–19  Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln]] in the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Cornhuskers were led by seventh-year coach head coach [[Tim Miles]] and played their home games at [[Pinnacle Bank Arena]] in [[Lincoln, Nebraska]] as members of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. They finished the season 19–17, 6–14 in [[2018–19 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in 13th place. In the [[2019 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they defeated [[2018–19 Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball team|Rutgers]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/rutgersbasketball/2019/03/rutgers-nebraska-big-ten-tournament.html|title=Rutgers ousted from Big Ten tournament as Nebraska delivers gut-punch in 2nd half|last=Sargeant|first=Keith|date=2019-03-14|website=nj.com|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-29}}</ref> and [[2018–19 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team|Maryland]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.omaha.com/huskers/mens-basketball/nebraska-beats-maryland-to-keep-big-ten-tournament-run-alive/article_df506d87-8fb3-5b17-9040-b6297b700b9a.html|title=Nebraska beats Maryland to keep Big Ten tournament run alive|first=Chris|last=Heady|website=Omaha.com|language=en|access-date=2019-04-29}}</ref> to advance to the quarterfinals where they lost to [[2018–19 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/uw/2019/03/15/wisconsin-66-nebraska-62-badgers-advance-big-ten-semifinals/3162895002/|title=Wisconsin advances to Big Ten semifinals despite flawed performance that included 17 turnovers|website=Milwaukee Journal Sentinel|language=en|access-date=2019-04-29}}</ref> They received an at-large bid to the [[2019 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]] where they defeated [[2018–19 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team|Butler]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401123727|title=Butler vs. Nebraska - Game Recap - March 20, 2019 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|language=en|access-date=2019-04-29}}</ref> in the first round before losing to [[2018–19 TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball team|TCU]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/college/big-12/texas-christian-university/article228365489.html|title=TCU continues winning NIT ways by crushing Nebraska. 'It's a special time of year'|last=By|website=star-telegram|language=en|access-date=2019-04-29}}</ref>

On March 26, 2019, Tim Miles was fired.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://journalstar.com/sports/huskers/mens-basketball/tim-miles-out-after-seven-seasons-as-nebraska-basketball-coach/article_f9645b9e-340f-5562-bc3e-228d3b9950b4.html|title=Tim Miles out after seven seasons as Nebraska basketball coach; Moos wants consistency in program|last=Basnett|first=Chris|website=JournalStar.com|language=en|access-date=2019-07-17}}</ref> Four days later, the school hired former [[Chicago Bulls]]' head coach [[Fred Hoiberg]] as the next head coach.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-basketball-ncaa-neb-hoiberg-idUSKCN1RB0LX|title=Nebraska hires Hoiberg to seven-year deal|date=2019-03-30|work=Reuters|access-date=2019-04-29|language=en}}</ref>

==Previous season==
The [[2017–18 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Cornhuskers]] finished the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2017–18 season]] 2211, 13–5 in [[2017–18 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in a tie for fourth place. As the No. 4 seed in the [[2018 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they lost in the quarterfinals to [[2017–18 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]]. Despite winning 13 Big Ten games, the Cornhuskers did not receive a bid to the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], but did receive a bid to the [[2018 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]]. However, they lost in the first round of the NIT to [[2017–18 Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball team|Mississippi State]].

==Schedule and results==
The 2018–19 season marked the first time in Big Ten history that the teams will play a 20-game conference schedule, setting a precedent for all Division I basketball.<ref name=":02">{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/big-ten-adds-two-games-for-a-20-game-conference-schedule-starting-in-2018-19/|title=Big Ten adds two games for a 20-game conference schedule starting in 2018–19 |last=Norlander|first=Matt|date=October 19, 2017|work=CBS Sports|access-date=March 9, 2018}}</ref> The new schedule also included a regional component to increase the frequency of games among teams in similar areas. Over the course of a six-year cycle (12 playing opportunities), in-state rivals will play each other 12 times, regional opponents will play 10 times, and all other teams will play nine times.<ref name=":02" /> Three in-state series will be guaranteed home-and-homes: Illinois and Northwestern, Indiana and Purdue, and Michigan and Michigan State will always play twice.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/21076233/big-ten-play-20-game-conference-schedule-next-season|title=Big Ten to move to 20-game conference slate |work=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-03-12}}</ref>

The Cornhuskers notably beat in-state rival Creighton 94–75 in the 2018–19 season for the first time since the 2010–11 season.

Nebraska again participated in the [[Gavitt Tipoff Games]] where they defeated [[2018–19 Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball team|Seton Hall]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.btpowerhouse.com/2018/5/15/17355414/2018-gavitt-games-big-ten-big-east-challenge-complete-schedule-matchups-games-dates-times-winner-tv|title=2018 Gavitt Games (Big Ten - Big East Challenge) Schedule|work=BT Powerhouse|access-date=2018-05-15}}</ref> The Cornuskers also participated in the [[CBE Hall of Fame Classic]] on November 19 and 20, at the [[Sprint Center]] in [[Kansas City, Missouri]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.halloffameweekend.com/classic/news/2018/2018_field|title=Hall of Fame Classic Announces 2018 Field|date=2018-03-06|work=Hall of Fame Weekend|access-date=2018-05-15|language=en}}</ref> Fellow participants in the tournament included [[2018–19 Missouri State Bears basketball team|Missouri State]], [[2018–19 Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball team|Texas Tech]], and [[2018–19 USC Trojans men's basketball team|USC]].
